tool.name: segemehl
tool.command:
## segemehl recognises gzip-compressed queries purely by the '.gz' filename suffix, while ## Galaxy stores datasets as 'dataset_N.dat'. Link gzipped queries to a name carrying that ## suffix before mapping, otherwise segemehl silently mis-parses them. #set $is_single = str( $library.type ) == 'single' #set $reads1 = str( $library.input_query ) if $is_single else str( $library.first_strand_query ) #set $reads2 = '' if $is_single else str( $library.second_strand_query ) #set $ext1 = $library.input_query.ext if $is_single else $library.first_strand_query.ext #set $ext2 = '' if $is_single else $library.second_strand_query.ext #if $ext1.endswith( '.gz' ) ln -sf "$reads1" query_1.fastq.gz && #set $reads1 = 'query_1.fastq.gz' #end if #if $ext2.endswith( '.gz' ) ln -sf '$reads2' query_2.fastq.gz && ln -sf '$reads1' query_1.fastq.gz && #set $reads1 = 'query_1.fastq.gz' #end if #if $ext2.endswith( '.gz' ) ln -sf '$reads2' query_2.fastq.gz && #end if
## build a segemehl index on the fly when the reference genome is supplied from the history #if $refGenomeSource.genomeSource == "history": mkdir ./temp_index/ && #set $temp_index = './temp_index/temp.idx' segemehl.x -x $temp_index -d '$refGenomeSource.own_reference_genome' && #else: #set $temp_index = $refGenomeSource.index.fields.index_path #end if
segemehl.x -t "\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-4}"
#if $refGenomeSource.genomeSource == "history": -d '${refGenomeSource.own_reference_genome}' #else: -d '${refGenomeSource.index.fields.db_path}' #end if
-i $temp_index
## single/paired-end reads; segemehl accepts exactly one query (-q) and one mate (-p) file #if $is_single: -q $reads1 #else -q $reads1 -p $reads2 -I $library.maxpairinsertsize #end if
#if str( $bisulfite ) != "0": -F $bisulfite #end if -m $minsize -A $accuracy -H $hitstrategy #if $maxout: -r $maxout #end if ## -S enables split-read mapping and takes an optional report basename. Without a basename the ## sidecar .sngl.bed/.mult.bed/.trns.txt reports are named after the -o output; those extra ## reports are not collected as Galaxy datasets. #if str( $splitreads.splits ) == "splits": -S -W $splitreads.minsplicecover -U $splitreads.minfragscore -Z $splitreads.minfraglen -l $splitreads.splicescorescale -w $splitreads.maxsplitevalue #end if -M $maxinterval -E $evalue -D $differences -J $jump -o '$segemehl_out' #if str( $nomatchfilename ) == 'yes': -u '$segemehl_outunmatched' #end if

param.label: Will you select a reference genome from your history or use a built-in index?
param.help: Built-ins were indexed using default options

param.name: index
param.label: Select a reference genome
param.help: If your genome of interest is not listed, contact your Galaxy admin

validator.message: No indexes are available for the selected input dataset

param.label: Maximum size of the inserts (paired end)
Min score of a spliced fragment
Min length of a spliced fragment
Report spliced alignment with score greater than this scale times the score
param.help: Report only if this value x score is larger than next best spliced alignment

param.label: Bisulfite mapping
param.option: Bisulfite mapping with methylC-seq/Lister et al.

param.label: Maximum number of alignments that will be reported
Min percentage of matches per read in semi-global alignment
Search seeds initially with n differences
Maximum width of a suffix array interval, i.e. a query seed will be omitted if it matches more than n times

tool.help:
**What it does**
Segemehl is a short read mapper with gaps.
Segemehl maps short sequencer reads to reference genomes. Unlike other methods, segemehl is able to detect not only mismatches but also insertions and deletions. Furthermore, segemehl is not limited to a specific read length and is able to map primer- or polyadenylation contaminated reads correctly. segemehl implements a matching strategy based on enhanced suffix arrays (ESA) and supports bisulfite sequencing mapping and split read mapping.
-----
**Inputs**
Reads can be given as FASTQ or FASTA, plain or gzip-compressed. Paired-end libraries are supplied as one first-strand and one second-strand file. The reference genome is either taken from the history (uncompressed FASTA, the index is then built on the fly) or from a pre-built segemehl index installed by your Galaxy administrator.
-----
**Outputs**
The main output is a SAM alignment file. Optionally the unmapped reads can be written to a separate FASTQ file.
When split-read detection is enabled, segemehl additionally writes BED-style split reports (`*.sngl.bed`, `*.mult.bed`) and a transcript table (`*.trns.txt`) next to the SAM file. These extra reports are not collected as Galaxy datasets.
